name: Government
topics: Basic concepts: power, authority, legitimacy and sovereignty
Separation of powers and checks and balances
Rule of law, rights of citizens and civil liberties
Organs of government: legislature, executive and judiciary
Nationalism and constitutional development to independence
Post-independence, military rule and return to democracy
Nigeria's foreign policy and international organisations

questions.q: In Government, 'power' is best defined as:
o: the ability to influence or control the behaviour of others, even against their will
the supreme authority of a state over its territory
the legal right to rule a state
the recognition given to a ruler by his people
questions.e: Power is the capacity to make people act in a certain way, whether they agree or not. It does not need to be legal or accepted to exist, unlike authority or legitimacy.
questions.p: Power na the fit to make people do wetin you want, even if dem no agree. E no need to be legal or dem to accept am before e dey there.

questions.q: Authority is different from mere power mainly because authority:
o: exists only in a democratic system of government
is always backed by military force
is the legitimate right to exercise power and command obedience
cannot be challenged by any citizen
questions.e: Authority is power that is recognised as lawful or rightful. A person in authority is obeyed because people accept his right to command, not just because he can force them.
questions.p: Authority na power wey people accept say e correct. Dem dey obey the person because dem believe say e get the right to command, no be say na only force e dey use.

questions.q: Legitimacy in government refers to:
o: the ability to use force to control citizens
the general acceptance by the people that a government has the right to rule
the independence of a state from foreign control
the power to make laws for a country
questions.e: Legitimacy means the people see a government's rule as rightful and proper, usually because it followed accepted rules like free elections or tradition.
questions.p: Legitimacy na when the citizens agree say the government get correct right to dey rule, mostly because the government follow accepted process like free election.

questions.q: Sovereignty, as used in Government studies, is best described as:
o: the right of citizens to vote during elections
the influence a leader has over members of his cabinet
the ability of a government to collect taxes from citizens
the supreme and final authority within a state
questions.e: Sovereignty is the highest and final authority in a state, above which there is no other power, either inside the country or from outside, that the state must obey.
questions.p: Sovereignty na the highest and final power for inside one state, no other power — whether from inside or outside — fit control am.

questions.q: Which situation best illustrates the external sovereignty of Nigeria as a state?
o: The President appointing ministers to head government ministries
The judiciary interpreting the provisions of the 1999 Constitution
The National Assembly making laws for the whole federation
Nigeria's independence from control by Britain or any other foreign power
questions.e: External sovereignty means a state is free from control by any outside power and relates freely with other nations as an equal. Nigeria's independence from Britain shows this freedom from foreign control.
questions.p: External sovereignty mean say no foreign country fit control the state again. Nigeria wey don free from Britain control na clear example of external sovereignty.

questions.q: A state's internal sovereignty is shown when the government:
o: exercises supreme authority over all persons and groups within its own territory
signs a trade treaty with another country
joins an international body like the African Union
receives diplomatic recognition from other nations
questions.e: Internal sovereignty concerns supreme control inside the state itself, over all citizens, institutions and groups within its borders. Treaties and recognition deal with external sovereignty, not internal.
questions.p: Internal sovereignty na when government get final power for inside im own territory, over all the people and groups dem. Treaty and recognition na external sovereignty matter.

questions.q: Major Danjuma took over the government of a fictional West African country through a military coup. He fully controls the armed forces and can enforce his orders, but most citizens see his government as unlawful and refuse to cooperate with it. This situation best shows that Major Danjuma has:
o: sovereignty without authority
power without legitimacy
authority without power
legitimacy without power
questions.e: Danjuma can force obedience (power) because he controls the army, but the people do not accept his rule as rightful, so he lacks legitimacy. This is a classic case of power without legitimacy.
questions.p: Danjuma get the army so e fit force people to obey am — na power. But the citizens no gree say im rule correct, so e no get legitimacy. Na power without legitimacy be dis.

questions.q: In a certain country, the constitution clearly states that the National Assembly holds supreme law-making power. In practice, however, powerful political godfathers and pressure groups actually decide most government policies behind the scenes. This situation best illustrates the difference between:
o: internal sovereignty and external sovereignty
de jure government and de facto government
legal sovereignty and political sovereignty
power and legitimacy
questions.e: Legal sovereignty is the authority officially recognised by the constitution or law (the National Assembly). Political sovereignty is the real, actual power behind government decisions (the godfathers/pressure groups), which may differ from who holds power on paper.
questions.p: Legal sovereignty na the power wey constitution talk say National Assembly get on paper. Political sovereignty na the real power wey dey behind the scene — for dis case na the godfathers and pressure groups. Na so e different be dis.

questions.q: Which of these is the most essential feature of a federal system of government?
o: Regional governments can secede whenever they wish
The central government appoints all regional governors
Powers are constitutionally divided between central and component units
A single legislature controls the whole country
questions.e: Federalism is defined by a written constitution that shares powers between the central government and the states or regions, with each level having areas of exclusive and concurrent authority.
questions.p: Federalism na when constitution share power between central government and di states, each one get im own area wey e dey control.

questions.q: A confederation differs from a federation mainly because, in a confederation,
o: the constitution of a confederation cannot be amended
there is no form of central authority whatsoever
the central government has supreme control over member states
member states retain greater sovereignty and may withdraw from the union
questions.e: In a confederation, member states remain largely independent and sovereign, joining together mainly for common interests like defence or trade, and may leave the union if they choose, unlike a federation where the centre has stronger constitutional control.
questions.p: For confederation, di member states still dey independent well-well, dem just join for common interest like defence or trade, and dem fit comot anytime, unlike federation wey centre get more power.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of the presidential system of government practised in Nigeria's Fourth Republic?
o: The President is a member of the legislature and answers to it
The executive and legislative arms are separate, with the President serving a fixed tenure
A Prime Minister heads government while a separate Head of State exists
The executive can be removed through a vote of no confidence
questions.e: Under a presidential system, there is separation of powers: the President is both Head of State and Government, elected for a fixed term, and is not a member of the National Assembly. This differs from the parliamentary system.
questions.p: For presidential system, power dey separate: President na Head of State and Government, dem dey elect am for fixed term, e no be member of National Assembly. Na different from parliamentary system.

questions.q: In a parliamentary system of government, such as practised in the United Kingdom, which statement best explains the relationship between the executive and the legislature?
o: There is strict separation of powers with independent tenure for both arms
There is a fusion of powers, as the Prime Minister and Cabinet are drawn from and remain accountable to Parliament
The Head of State is directly elected by the people for a fixed term
Members of the executive cannot also sit in the legislature
questions.e: Parliamentary systems operate on fusion of powers: the Prime Minister and ministers are usually elected members of Parliament and must retain its confidence to remain in office, unlike the strict separation found in presidential systems.
questions.p: Parliamentary system dey work with fusion of power: Prime Minister and ministers na members of Parliament, and dem must get Parliament support to remain for office, no be like presidential system wey power dey separate well-well.

questions.q: A form of government in which the Head of State inherits the position by birth right, as with a traditional Oba in Yorubaland, is known as:
o: Monarchy
Aristocracy
Oligarchy
Theocracy
questions.e: Monarchy is a system where leadership passes down through royal bloodline or inheritance, as seen in traditional kingship institutions like the Oba, Emir, or Obi.
questions.p: Monarchy na system wey leadership dey pass through royal blood or inheritance, like traditional king institutions - Oba, Emir, or Obi.

questions.q: A government in which political authority is believed to come from, and is exercised strictly according to, religious laws is called:
o: Plutocracy
Technocracy
Theocracy
Autocracy
questions.e: Theocracy is rule guided by religious doctrine, where religious leaders or laws determine governance, unlike autocracy (rule by one person) or plutocracy (rule by the wealthy).
questions.p: Theocracy na when religion dey guide how dem dey rule, religious leaders or laws dey determine governance, e no be like autocracy (one person rule) or plutocracy (rich people rule).

questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest indicator that a country operates a one-party dictatorship rather than a multi-party democracy?
o: Only one political party is legally permitted to contest and win elections
The Head of State addresses the nation during elections
Citizens pay taxes to only one government agency
The country operates under a written constitution
questions.e: The true mark of a one-party dictatorship is that the law bans competing parties, so citizens have no real choice at elections. Having a constitution or a single tax agency does not by itself prove dictatorship.
questions.p: Di real sign of one-party dictatorship na say law no gree make other parties contest, so citizens no get real choice for election. To get constitution or one tax agency no mean say na dictatorship automatically.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a constitution?
o: A set of customs followed by traditional rulers in a community
A set of laws made only by the legislature
A document containing only the fundamental rights of citizens
The body of rules and principles that guide the governance of a state
questions.e: A constitution is the general body of rules and principles by which a state is governed, covering the structure and powers of government as well as citizens' rights. It is broader than just laws from the legislature or a rights-only document.
questions.p: Constitution na di general rules and principles wey dem dey use govern one kontri. E no be just laws wey legislature pass or only about citizens right, e cover everything about how government go work.

questions.q: Which of these countries is commonly cited as an example of a country with an unwritten constitution?
o: The Federal Republic of Nigeria
Great Britain
The United States of America
The Republic of Ghana
questions.e: Britain's constitution is not contained in one single document; it is made up of statutes, conventions, judicial decisions and customs built over time. Nigeria, the USA and Ghana all have their constitutions written in a single formal document.
questions.p: Britain constitution no dey inside one document, na combination of laws, customs, court judgements and tradition wey don grow over time. Nigeria, USA and Ghana get their own written down for one document.

questions.q: A constitution is said to be rigid when it has which of these features?
o: It applies only to members of the executive arm of government
It can be amended through the ordinary law-making process
It is not written down in any single document
Its amendment requires a special and more difficult procedure than ordinary laws
questions.e: A rigid constitution needs a special, often more difficult, procedure (like special majorities) to amend, unlike ordinary laws which pass through the normal legislative process. This makes it harder to change than regular statutes.
questions.p: Rigid constitution na di one wey dem need special and harder process to change, e no be like normal law wey dem fit change anyhow. Na why e dey different from ordinary laws.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes the meaning of constitutionalism?
o: Government conducted strictly within the limits and principles laid down by the constitution
The process by which a new constitution is drafted and adopted
The power of a Head of State to suspend the constitution during emergencies
The mere existence of a written constitution in a country
questions.e: Constitutionalism means that government and its officials operate within the limits set by the constitution, respecting the rule of law and citizens' rights. Simply having a written constitution does not guarantee this if the rules are ignored in practice.
questions.p: Constitutionalism mean say government and dem officials dey rule according to wetin constitution talk, dem go respect rule of law and people rights. To just get written constitution no mean say dem dey follow am well well.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, if an Act of the National Assembly conflicts with a provision of the Constitution, what happens to that Act?
o: The President decides which of the two should be obeyed
It automatically becomes part of the Constitution
It is void to the extent of its inconsistency with the Constitution
It remains valid until the Senate President cancels it
questions.e: The Constitution is supreme, so any law that conflicts with it is null and void only to the extent of that inconsistency, while the rest of the law may still stand. This is a key feature of constitutional supremacy.
questions.p: Constitution na di highest law, so any law wey no match am go be useless for di part wey no agree with am, but di other parts fit still dey work. Na so constitutional supremacy dey work.

questions.q: Which of these is a major requirement for amending the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria?
o: The signature of the Chief Justice of Nigeria alone
Two-thirds majority vote of each House of the National Assembly plus a resolution by at least two-thirds of all State Houses of Assembly
A national referendum conducted by INEC without any involvement of the legislature
A simple majority vote of members present at a National Assembly sitting
questions.e: Amending the 1999 Constitution requires a two-thirds majority in both the Senate and House of Representatives, plus approval by at least two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly. This strict, layered process is why the constitution is described as rigid.
questions.p: To change 1999 Constitution, Senate and House of Reps go need two-third majority, and at least two-third out of di 36 State Houses of Assembly must agree too. Na dis strict process make di constitution rigid.

questions.q: In a certain West African country, the constitution guarantees freedom from arbitrary arrest, yet security agents regularly detain critics of the government without trial and the courts' orders for their release are ignored. This situation best illustrates which of the following?
o: Federalism being practised effectively
The existence of a constitution without constitutionalism
True constitutionalism in practice
A flexible constitution in operation
questions.e: Having a written constitution with rights on paper is not the same as constitutionalism, which requires government to actually respect and be limited by those rules. Ignoring court orders and detaining people unlawfully shows a constitution exists but constitutionalism is absent.
questions.p: To just get constitution wey talk about freedom no mean say constitutionalism dey ground, because constitutionalism na when government dey follow di rules for real. If dem dey detain people anyhow and ignore court, na constitution dey but constitutionalism no dey.

questions.q: Who is generally regarded as the father of the modern theory of separation of powers through his book, 'The Spirit of Laws'?
o: Baron de Montesquieu
John Locke
Thomas Hobbes
Jean-Jacques Rousseau
questions.e: Baron de Montesquieu, a French philosopher, developed the modern theory of separation of powers in his book 'The Spirit of Laws'. He argued that liberty is best protected when the legislature, executive and judiciary are kept separate.
questions.p: Montesquieu na the French thinker wey develop the modern theory of separation of powers for im book 'The Spirit of Laws'. E talk say liberty go dey safe well well if legislature, executive and judiciary no dey for one hand.

questions.q: Which arm of government is constitutionally responsible for making laws in Nigeria?
o: The Civil Service
The Executive
The Judiciary
The Legislature
questions.e: The legislature (National Assembly at the federal level or House of Assembly at the state level) is the arm saddled with law-making. The executive implements laws while the judiciary interprets them.
questions.p: Na the legislature (National Assembly or House of Assembly) dey make laws. Executive na im dey carry out the laws, while judiciary dey interpret am.

questions.q: The theory of separation of powers states that the three arms of government should be headed by
o: the same person to ensure unity
members of one political party only
different persons to prevent abuse of power
traditional rulers appointed by the state
questions.e: The theory insists that different persons should head the legislature, executive and judiciary so that no single person or group controls the whole government, thereby checking abuse of power.
questions.p: The theory talk say make different people head the three arms, so that one person no go control everything, and this one go prevent misuse of power.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the principle of checks and balances in government?
o: The ability of each arm of government to control the excesses of the others
The fusion of the legislature and executive into one single body
Complete separation of the three arms with no contact among them
The total independence of the judiciary from the constitution
questions.e: Checks and balances means each arm of government has some power to monitor and control the activities of the other arms, so that none of them becomes too powerful or abuses office.
questions.p: Checks and balances mean say each arm of government get small power to control the oda arms, so that no arm go too powerful or misuse im office.

questions.q: In a presidential system of government, which of these powers is a legislative check on the executive?
o: The power to declare an act of the legislature unconstitutional
The power to screen and confirm ministerial nominees
The power to grant state pardon
The power to appoint judges
questions.e: Screening and confirming ministerial or other presidential nominees by the legislature limits the executive's power of appointment; the other options belong to the executive or judiciary, not the legislature.
questions.p: When legislature dey screen and confirm minister wey president nominate, na legislative check on executive im appointment power; the oda options na executive or judiciary powers.

questions.q: Which power allows the judiciary to check the excesses of the legislature and the executive?
o: Power of appropriation
Power of veto
Power of impeachment
Power of judicial review
questions.e: Judicial review is the power of the courts to examine laws made by the legislature or actions taken by the executive and declare them null and void if they conflict with the constitution.
questions.p: Judicial review na the power wey court get to check law wey legislature pass or wetin executive do, and cancel am if e no follow constitution.

questions.q: Governor Audu refused to sign a bill passed by his State House of Assembly into law. The House, however, gathered a two-thirds majority and passed the bill into law without his assent. This scenario best illustrates
o: Executive supremacy
Fusion of powers
Legislative override of executive veto
Judicial activism
questions.e: When a legislature uses a two-thirds majority to pass a bill into law despite the governor's refusal to sign it, it is overriding the executive veto, which is a clear example of a legislative check on the executive.
questions.p: When the House use two-thirds majority pass bill become law even after governor refuse to sign, na legislature don override the executive veto; na legislative check on executive be dat.

questions.q: A major weakness of a strict application of separation of powers in government is that it may lead to
o: Quick decision-making between the arms
Total elimination of corruption in government
Concentration of power in one arm of government
Conflict and deadlock between the arms of government
questions.e: Strict separation of powers can make the arms of government act independently without cooperating, which may cause disagreement and deadlock, especially on policies or appointments that require joint action.
questions.p: If the three arms separate too much without cooperation, e fit cause wahala and deadlock, especially when dem no gree for one policy or appointment.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the principle of 'Rule of Law'?
o: The law is supreme and applies equally to everyone, including government officials
The military can rule a country through decrees instead of the constitution
The government has the right to detain citizens without trial during emergencies
Courts are allowed to make new laws whenever they judge a case
questions.e: The Rule of Law means that no person, including those in government, is above the law, and everyone is subject to the same legal rules and processes. The other options describe actions that go against this principle.
questions.p: Rule of Law mean say law dey reign for everybody, even government people no fit dodge am. The other options na things wey dey against this idea, like detaining person anyhow or military dey rule with decree.

questions.q: The doctrine of the Rule of Law, as commonly taught in Government studies, is most closely associated with which scholar?
o: Baron de Montesquieu
A.V. Dicey
Jean Jacques Rousseau
John Locke
questions.e: A.V. Dicey, a British constitutional lawyer, is widely credited with developing and popularising the doctrine of the Rule of Law in the 19th century. Montesquieu is known for separation of powers, Locke for natural rights, and Rousseau for social contract theory.
questions.p: A.V. Dicey na the man wey dem sabi for Rule of Law teaching, he explain am well for him book. Montesquieu na separation of powers, Locke na natural rights, Rousseau na social contract.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a recognised feature of the Rule of Law?
o: Supremacy of the law over all persons
Protection of fundamental human rights by the courts
Arbitrary arrest and detention of citizens without due process
Equality of all citizens before the law
questions.e: Arbitrary arrest without due process is exactly what the Rule of Law seeks to prevent, since it violates fair hearing and personal liberty. The other three options are genuine features that uphold the Rule of Law.
questions.p: Arbitrary arrest without due process na the kind thing wey Rule of Law dey fight against, because e dey spoil fair hearing and personal freedom. The other three na real things wey Rule of Law dey support.

questions.q: Chief Nduka, a wealthy businessman in Onitsha, was arrested for fraud and tried in court using the same procedure applied to an ordinary trader accused of a similar offence. This situation best illustrates which principle of the Rule of Law?
o: Doctrine of necessity
Federal character principle
Separation of powers
Equality before the law
questions.e: Equality before the law means that no one, regardless of wealth or status, receives special treatment in the eyes of the law. Chief Nduka being tried like an ordinary person shows this principle in action.
questions.p: Equality before the law mean say everybody, no matter how rich or big dem be, go face law the same way. Chief Nduka wey dem try like ordinary trader na clear example of dis.

questions.q: Which of the following rights is classified as a fundamental human right enforceable in a Nigerian court, unlike directive principles of state policy?
o: Right to personal liberty
Right to a minimum living wage
Right to free university education
Right to guaranteed employment
questions.e: Right to personal liberty is a fundamental human right guaranteed and enforceable under the Constitution. Free education, employment and minimum wage are socio-economic goals under directive principles, which are not directly enforceable in court.
questions.p: Right to personal liberty na fundamental right wey person fit carry go court make dem enforce am. Free education, work, and minimum wage na just government goals (directive principles) wey court no dey force like dat.

questions.q: Which legal writ is used to compel the authorities holding a person in custody to bring that person before a court and justify the detention?
o: Quo warranto
Mandamus
Habeas corpus
Certiorari
questions.e: Habeas corpus is a court order that requires detaining authorities to produce the detained person and explain the legal grounds for the detention. This protects citizens from unlawful or secret imprisonment.
questions.p: Habeas corpus na court order wey dem dey use force people wey dey hold person for custody make dem bring am come court and explain why dem dey hold am. E dey protect person from secret or illegal detention.

questions.q: During a peaceful demonstration in Kano over fuel price increase, security agents dispersed the protesters with force and detained several of them for two weeks without any court order or charge. Which civil liberties were most directly violated in this scenario?
o: Right to own property only
Right to personal liberty and freedom of assembly
Right to fair hearing only
Right to freedom of worship only
questions.e: Detaining the protesters for two weeks without court order violates their right to personal liberty, while dispersing a peaceful protest violates their right to freedom of assembly. Property and worship were not the main issues in this scenario.
questions.p: Dem detain the protesters for two weeks without court order, dat one touch personal liberty; and dem scatter peaceful protest, dat one touch freedom of assembly. Property and worship no be wetin dis case dey about.

questions.q: Which of the following represents a LAWFUL limitation of civil liberties under the Rule of Law, rather than a violation of citizens' rights?
o: A state of emergency is properly declared following constitutional procedure, temporarily restricting movement in a conflict zone
A government bans a political party without following any court process
The police detain a suspect for several months without charging the person to court
A state governor dissolves the judiciary in his state by executive order
questions.e: A properly declared state of emergency, following the constitution, is a recognised legal way to temporarily limit certain freedoms for public safety, so it is lawful. The other options describe actions that bypass due process and are therefore violations of the Rule of Law.
questions.p: When dem follow constitution declare state of emergency well-well, e dey legal to limit some freedom small for public safety. The other options na pure violation because dem skip due process entirely.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a political party?
o: A court-appointed body that settles disputes between citizens
A group of wealthy individuals who meet to discuss business opportunities
An organised group of people who share similar beliefs and aim to win political power through elections
A club formed by civil servants to negotiate salary increases
questions.e: A political party is an organised group with a common ideology that seeks to gain control of government by winning elections. The other options describe economic, social or judicial bodies, not political parties.
questions.p: Political party na organised group wey share same belief and wan rule kontri through election. Di oda ones na business, work union or court matter, dem no be political party.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature of a one-party system of government?
o: Many parties compete freely for votes during elections
Only one political party is legally allowed to exist and contest elections
Political parties are banned while the military rules directly
Two strong parties take turns to form government
questions.e: In a one-party system, the law permits only a single party to operate, so there is no room for other parties to contest elections. This is different from a multi-party or two-party system where more than one party competes.
questions.p: For one-party system, na only one party de law allow make e dey operate and contest election. E different from multi-party or two-party system wey get plenty parties de compete.

questions.q: Which country is widely recognised as a classic example of the two-party system, where two major parties have dominated national politics for a long time?
o: Nigeria during the Fourth Republic
Federal Republic of Nigeria under military rule
People's Republic of China
United States of America
questions.e: The USA is a classic two-party state because the Democratic Party and Republican Party have dominated its politics for a very long time, even though smaller parties exist. China has one dominant party, while Nigeria's Fourth Republic has several active parties.
questions.p: USA na classic two-party kontri because Democratic Party and Republican Party don dey control dia politics for long time, even though small parties dey. China get only one strong party, Nigeria Fourth Republic get plenty parties.

questions.q: Which of these statements correctly describes a multi-party system of government?
o: Parties are forbidden from campaigning in public places
Only two parties are allowed to contest any election
A single party rules without any form of opposition
Several political parties exist and may form coalitions to govern
questions.e: A multi-party system allows several parties to exist and contest elections, and since no single party may win an outright majority, parties often form coalition governments. The other options describe one-party or two-party features, not multi-party systems.
questions.p: Multi-party system mean say plenty parties dey exist and dem fit contest election, and since one party fit no win outright majority, dem fit join hand form coalition government. Di oda options na one-party or two-party features.

questions.q: During Nigeria's Second Republic (1979-1983), five major parties — NPN, UPN, NPP, GNPP and PRP — contested national elections, each drawing support from different regions. This arrangement best illustrates which type of party system?
o: Dominant single-party system
Two-party system
Multi-party system
One-party system
questions.e: Having five active parties contesting elections at the same time, with none enjoying a legal monopoly, shows a multi-party system. This is unlike a two-party system, which has only two major contenders, or a one-party system, which allows just one party.
questions.p: Since five parties (NPN, UPN, NPP, GNPP, PRP) dey contest election togeda, with no party wey get sole right to rule, na multi-party system be dat. E no be two-party (wey get only two big parties) or one-party (wey get only one party).

questions.q: Which of the following is a major function of political parties in a democratic society?
o: Selecting and presenting candidates for public elective offices
Issuing national identity cards to citizens
Printing and distributing the national currency
Collecting personal income tax from workers
questions.e: One core function of political parties is to screen and nominate candidates who will stand for election into public offices. Tax collection, ID cards and currency printing are government or agency functions, not party functions.
questions.p: One key work wey political party dey do na to select and present candidate wey go contest public office. Tax collection, ID card and money printing na government or agency work, no be party work.

questions.q: How does a political party mainly differ from a pressure group?
o: Political parties do not prepare manifestoes, but pressure groups do
A political party seeks to win elections and control government, while a pressure group only tries to influence government policy without seeking power
Pressure groups contest elections directly, while political parties only lobby government officials
A pressure group always has more registered members than any political party
questions.e: A political party's main goal is to win elections and form government, whereas a pressure group tries to influence government decisions without seeking to control power itself. The other options reverse or wrongly state the true relationship.
questions.p: Political party main aim na to win election and control government, but pressure group just dey try influence government decision without wanting to rule. Di oda options don mix up di correct relationship.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major criticism often raised against the one-party system of government?
o: It leads to wasteful spending because too many parties campaign at once
It encourages frequent change of government through coalition collapse
It makes elections too expensive due to the large number of contesting parties
It tends to promote dictatorship since there is no strong opposition to check the ruling party
questions.e: Because only one party is allowed in a one-party system, there is no organised opposition to challenge the ruling party's decisions, which can easily lead to abuse of power and dictatorship. The other options actually describe problems linked with multi-party systems, not one-party systems.
questions.p: Since na only one party dem allow for one-party system, no strong opposition dey to check di ruling party, and dis fit cause am to turn dictatorship. Di oda options na problem wey dey more common for multi-party system, no be one-party.

questions.q: A pressure group is best defined as a group of persons who organize themselves to:
o: Influence government decisions and policies without seeking to form government
Interpret the constitution for the courts
Make laws for the whole country
Seek political power by contesting elections
questions.e: A pressure group tries to influence government policy in favour of its members or a cause, but it does not contest elections to control government. That work belongs to political parties.
questions.p: Pressure group na people wey come together to push government make dem change policy, but dem no dey enter election to rule. Na political party dey do that one.

questions.q: Which of these organizations is a typical example of a pressure group in Nigeria?
o: Labour Party
Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC)
Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)
All Progressives Congress (APC)
questions.e: NLC is a trade union that pushes for workers' welfare through pressure on government, not through contesting elections. The other three options are registered political parties.
questions.p: NLC na workers union wey dey push government for better welfare, e no dey contest election. The other three na political parties wey dey canvass for votes.

questions.q: The main difference between a pressure group and a political party is that:
o: A political party has no leadership structure, unlike a pressure group
Pressure groups are illegal while political parties are legal
A pressure group seeks only to influence government policy, while a political party contests elections to control government
A pressure group is larger in membership than a political party
questions.e: Pressure groups lobby and pressure those in power to favour their interests, but they do not aim to capture government. Political parties specifically organize to win elections and run government.
questions.p: Pressure group just dey push government to favour dem interest, dem no wan rule. Political party dey organize to win election and control government.

questions.q: A group that is formed mainly to promote a cause of general public interest, such as environmental protection or anti-corruption, rather than to protect the welfare of its own paid-up members, is called a:
o: Cabinet committee
Promotional (attitude) group
Civil service board
Sectional (interest) group
questions.e: Promotional groups campaign for broad causes that benefit society in general, such as the environment, human rights, or anti-corruption. Sectional groups, unlike promotional groups, protect the specific interests of their own members such as workers or professionals.
questions.p: Promotional group dey fight for general cause wey go benefit everybody, like environment or anti-corruption. Sectional group na for dem own members' interest, like workers union.

questions.q: Public opinion can best be described as:
o: The collective view or judgement held by the majority of people on a given public issue
Laws passed by the National Assembly
Decisions handed down by the Supreme Court
The personal opinion of the Head of State on national issues
questions.e: Public opinion is the shared view of a significant number of people in society about a particular matter of common concern. It is not the view of one person or an arm of government.
questions.p: Public opinion na the view wey majority of people share about one public matter. E no be one person im view or government body own.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT usually regarded as an agent that shapes public opinion in a society?
o: Religious institutions
The family
Mass media (radio, television, newspapers)
Daily weather pattern
questions.e: Mass media, religion and family regularly influence how people think and form views about issues. Weather pattern has no direct role in shaping people's opinions on public matters.
questions.p: Mass media, religion and family dey always shape as people dey think about public matter. Weather no get anything to do with how people dey form opinion.

questions.q: When the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) wants government to improve funding of public universities, which method is it most likely to use as a pressure group?
o: Dissolving the National Assembly
Contesting for the office of the President
Embarking on a strike action to press home its demands
Appointing new Vice-Chancellors directly
questions.e: Pressure groups commonly use strikes, protests, petitions and lobbying to force government to listen to their demands. Contesting elections, dissolving the legislature, or appointing officials are not powers that pressure groups have.
questions.p: Pressure group like ASUU dey use strike, protest and lobbying to make government hear dem matter. Dem no get power to contest election, scatter National Assembly or appoint VC.

questions.q: A traders' association originally formed to protect members' business interests later decides to register formally, sponsor its own candidates, and contest elections at local and state levels. This association has most likely transformed into a:
o: Civil service commission
Electoral tribunal
Political party
Public opinion poll agency
questions.e: Once a group moves beyond lobbying and begins contesting elections to seek control of government, it has crossed the line from being a pressure group into becoming a political party. The key test is the aim to govern, not just to influence.
questions.p: Once group pass just lobbying come start to contest election to control government, e don turn political party. Na the aim to rule be the key sign, no be just to influence.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an 'electoral system'?
o: A set of laws guiding the conduct of civil servants
The method by which votes are cast and seats or offices are allocated to determine winners in an election
The body that supervises the conduct of a national population census
A register containing the names of all registered political parties
questions.e: An electoral system is simply the method or rule used to turn votes cast by voters into actual winners of seats or offices. It is not about civil servants, party registers, or census.
questions.p: Electoral system na di way wey dem dey use votes wey people cast decide who win election or seat. E no be about civil servant rules, party list, or census.

questions.q: In Nigeria, which body is constitutionally empowered to organize, undertake and supervise elections into the offices of President, Governors, and members of the National and State Assemblies?
o: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC)
Code of Conduct Bureau
National Population Commission
questions.e: INEC is the federal body set up by the Nigerian Constitution to conduct elections at the national level, including Presidential, Governorship and National/State Assembly elections. SIEC only handles Local Government elections, while the other two bodies have different functions entirely.
questions.p: INEC na di body wey Constitution give power to conduct election for President, Governor, National and State Assembly. SIEC na for Local Government election only, and di other two bodies no dey do election work at all.

questions.q: Under the Proportional Representation electoral system, seats in the legislature are mainly allocated to political parties based on:
o: The geographical size of the constituency
The seniority of each party's candidates
The number of years each party has existed
The percentage of total votes each party scores in the election
questions.e: Proportional Representation shares out legislative seats in proportion to the percentage of votes each party receives nationwide or in a region. This way, a party with 20% of votes gets roughly 20% of the seats, unlike First-Past-The-Post.
questions.p: Proportional Representation dey share seat for legislature based on di percentage of votes each party score. If party get 20% of votes, dem go roughly give am 20% of di seats, no be like First-Past-The-Post.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of an indirect election conducted through an Electoral College, instead of direct voting by the electorate?
o: Election of members of the Nigerian House of Representatives by direct adult suffrage
Election of the President of the United States by the Electoral College
Election of a Nigerian State Governor through direct adult suffrage
Election of a Nigerian Local Government Chairman by direct adult suffrage
questions.e: In the American system, ordinary voters actually choose 'electors' in each state, and it is these electors who formally elect the President; this is an indirect, Electoral College method. The other three options are all direct elections where voters themselves choose the winner.
questions.p: For America, di ordinary voters dey choose 'electors' for each state, and na dem go now officially vote President; dat one na indirect, Electoral College style. Di other three options na direct election wia voters demsef dey pick di winner.

questions.q: In a Federal Constituency election conducted under the First-Past-The-Post (FPTP) system, four candidates scored as follows out of 100,000 valid votes cast: Okafor - 35,000; Bello - 30,000; Yusuf - 20,000; Adeyemi - 15,000. Who should be declared the winner, and why?
o: Okafor, because he scored the highest number of votes, even though it is less than half of the total votes cast
No winner should be declared, since no candidate scored up to 50% of total votes
Bello, because his votes added to Yusuf's votes are greater than Okafor's votes
Adeyemi, because FPTP protects the interest of the smallest candidate
questions.e: FPTP declares the candidate with the highest single number of votes (a simple plurality) as winner, even if that number is less than 50% of total votes. Okafor's 35,000 is more than any other single candidate's score, so he wins, regardless of what other candidates' votes add up to.
questions.p: FPTP dey declare di candidate wey score di highest number of votes as winner, even if e no reach 50% of total votes. Okafor im 35,000 pass any other single candidate, so na im go win, no matter wetin di others add up to.

questions.q: A fresh election conducted to fill a legislative seat that becomes vacant between general elections, due to the death or resignation of the former occupant, is known as a:
o: Referendum
General election
By-election
Run-off election
questions.e: A by-election is held specifically to fill a single vacant seat that falls empty outside the normal election cycle, often because the former holder died, resigned, or was removed. It is different from a general election, which covers many seats at once.
questions.p: By-election na election wey dem conduct to fill one seat wey become empty before im time, maybe because di person wey dey hold am die, resign, or dem remove am. E different from general election wey cover plenty seats at once.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major pre-election function performed by an electoral body such as INEC?
o: Prosecuting corruption cases in the regular law courts
Approving the national budget presented by the Executive arm of government
Appointing ministers to the Federal Executive Council
Delimiting constituencies and compiling the voters' register
questions.e: Before any election, INEC must mark out constituency boundaries (delimitation) and prepare an accurate voters' register. Appointing ministers, prosecuting cases, and approving budgets belong to other arms of government, not the electoral body.
questions.p: Before any election, INEC must draw constituency boundary (delimitation) and prepare correct voters' register. To appoint minister, prosecute case, or approve budget na work for other arm of government, no be electoral body work.

questions.q: In a certain state, the ruling party deliberately redraws the boundaries of a constituency so that opposition supporters, who used to be concentrated together in one area, are now scattered across several other constituencies, making them a minority everywhere and reducing their chances of winning any seat. This practice is called:
o: Franchise
Gerrymandering
Suffrage
Delimitation
questions.e: Gerrymandering is the deliberate, unfair manipulation of constituency boundaries to give one party or group an electoral advantage over another. Ordinary delimitation is a neutral, lawful exercise, but when it is done dishonestly to weaken an opponent's voting strength, it becomes gerrymandering.
questions.p: Gerrymandering na wen dem purposely change constituency boundary anyhow to favour one party pass di other. Normal delimitation na fair work, but if dem do am dirty style to weaken opposition voters, dat one don turn gerrymandering.

questions.q: What is federalism, as practised in a country like Nigeria?
o: Government formed by independent states that retain full sovereignty and can withdraw at will
Government where all powers are concentrated at the centre
Government controlled entirely by traditional rulers and chiefs
Government in which power is shared between a central authority and constituent states, with each level supreme in its own sphere
questions.e: Federalism is a system where power is constitutionally divided between a central (federal) government and component states, and each level is supreme within its own area of authority. This is different from a unitary system (centre controls all) or a confederation (states keep full sovereignty).
questions.p: Federalism na system wey dem share power between central govment and di states, and each level get im own full power for im area. E no be like unitary wey everything dey centre, or confederation wey states still get full sovereignty.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a key feature of a unitary system of government?
o: A written constitution is strictly forbidden under this system
Component states retain the right to secede from the union at any time
All governmental powers are concentrated in a single central authority, which may delegate some functions to local units it can control or abolish
Two or more levels of government each with constitutionally guaranteed powers
questions.e: In a unitary system, supreme power lies with the central government. Local or regional bodies only exercise powers given to them by the centre, and the centre can change or remove such powers. This is unlike federalism, where states have guaranteed powers.
questions.p: For unitary system, all power dey for central govment. Local bodies dey only use power wey centre give dem, and centre fit change or remove am anytime. E no be like federalism wey states get guaranteed power.

questions.q: A confederation is best described as which type of political arrangement?
o: A loose union of independent sovereign states that cooperate on specific matters while each retains its own sovereignty
A division of powers between national and state governments under one written constitution
A military arrangement where soldiers rule without any constitution at all
A single central government that controls all regions directly with no autonomy for them
questions.e: A confederation is a weak, loose association formed by fully independent states to cooperate on limited common matters such as defence or trade, but each state keeps its full sovereignty and can leave the union. This is different from a federation, where states give up some sovereignty to a stronger central government.
questions.p: Confederation na loose union wey independent states form so dem fit work together for small matters like defence or trade, but every state still get im full power and fit comot anytime. E different from federation wey states give some power to strong central govment.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended), how many tiers of government operate in the federal structure?
o: One tier - a single central government for the whole country
Three tiers - federal, state and local governments
Two tiers only - federal and state governments
Four tiers - federal, state, local and traditional councils
questions.e: Nigeria's federal system, as set out in the 1999 Constitution, recognises three tiers of government: the Federal Government, the 36 State Governments, and the Local Government Councils. Traditional institutions are not a constitutional tier of government.
questions.p: Nigeria federal system, wey dem write for 1999 Constitution, get three tiers: Federal Govment, di 36 State Govments, and Local Govment Councils. Traditional rulers no be constitutional tier of govment.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine advantage of practising federalism in a country with many ethnic and religious groups, such as Nigeria?
o: It allows each component unit to manage its local affairs according to its own peculiar needs and interests
It reduces the total number of government workers needed nationwide
It removes the need for the country to have a written constitution
It concentrates all decision-making power at the centre for faster national decisions
questions.e: Federalism allows states or regions to control certain local matters that suit their own peculiar needs, such as local chieftaincy affairs, which helps manage diversity. The other options describe features of a unitary system or are simply untrue of federalism.
questions.p: Federalism allow states to handle their own local matters wey fit their peculiar need, like chieftaincy affairs, and e dey help manage diversity well. Di oda options na features of unitary system or dem just no correct for federalism.

questions.q: A student argues that federalism suits a large country with many different ethnic and religious groups better than a unitary system. Which reason best supports this argument?
o: Federalism ensures that only one dominant ethnic group fully controls the central government
Federalism requires every state to adopt the same official religion as the centre
Federalism removes the need for elections to be held in any of the component states
Federalism allows diverse groups to enjoy some self-governing autonomy in their states while still remaining united under one central government, which reduces fears of domination
questions.e: In a diverse country, federalism lets different groups control their own state affairs (such as education or local chieftaincy matters) while still being united nationally, which reduces fear that one group will dominate the others. This balance of unity and autonomy is federalism's main strength over a unitary system in such societies.
questions.p: For country wey get plenty different ethnic and religion groups, federalism allow make each group manage their own state affairs while dem still dey united as one nation, and dis one dey reduce fear say one group go dominate di oda ones. Na dis balance of unity and freedom be federalism main advantage pass unitary system for such society.

questions.q: Which feature most clearly distinguishes a confederation from a federation?
o: In a confederation, the central government has far more power than any member state
In a confederation, citizens owe allegiance only to the central authority and not to their own state
In a confederation, the member states retain supreme sovereignty and can lawfully withdraw from the union, unlike states in a true federation
In a confederation, there is only one single written constitution binding all members permanently
questions.e: The key legal difference is that confederate states never surrender their full sovereignty; they can leave the arrangement when they choose, because the union is based on an agreement among equals. In a federation, states give up some sovereignty permanently to a central government that they cannot simply withdraw from.
questions.p: Di main difference na say confederate states never give up their full sovereignty; dem fit comot from di union anytime because na agreement among equal states. But for federation, states don already give some sovereignty permanently to central govment and dem no fit just waka comot.

questions.q: Which of the following is often cited as a disadvantage of practising the federal system of government?
o: It automatically guarantees that resources will be shared equally among all states
It encourages fast, uniform decision-making for the whole country without delay
It can lead to duplication of government functions and offices, thereby increasing the overall cost of governance
It completely eliminates rivalry or competition among the component states
questions.e: Because federalism creates separate government structures (executive, legislature, civil service) at both the federal and state levels, many offices and functions are duplicated, which raises the cost of running government. The other options wrongly describe federalism as having unitary-type benefits it does not actually guarantee.
questions.p: Because federalism get separate govment structures (executive, legislature, civil service) for both federal and state level, plenty offices and functions dey duplicate, and dis one dey increase cost of governance. Di oda options dey wrongly give federalism benefits wey e no really guarantee.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the legislature in a democratic system of government?
o: Making laws for the state
Enforcing the laws of the land
Interpreting the laws made
Appointing judges to the courts
questions.e: The legislature is the law-making arm of government. It debates and passes bills which become laws when assented to. Enforcing and interpreting laws belong to the executive and judiciary respectively.
questions.p: Legislature na di arm wey dey make law for di kontri. Dem go discuss bill well-well before e go become law. To enforce or interpret law na for executive and judiciary.

questions.q: The Nigerian National Assembly is made up of the Senate and the House of Representatives, sitting as two separate chambers. What term best describes this type of legislature?
o: Unicameral legislature
Parliamentary legislature
Confederal legislature
Bicameral legislature
questions.e: A legislature with two chambers, like Nigeria's Senate and House of Representatives, is called bicameral. A unicameral legislature has only one chamber.
questions.p: Legislature wey get two chamber, like Senate and House of Reps for Nigeria, na bicameral. If na one chamber, dem go call am unicameral.

questions.q: Which arm of government is mainly responsible for interpreting the constitution and settling legal disputes between individuals or between individuals and the state?
o: The civil service
The judiciary
The legislature
The executive
questions.e: The judiciary is the arm of government that interprets laws and the constitution and resolves disputes through the courts. The legislature makes laws while the executive implements them.
questions.p: Na judiciary dey interpret constitution and settle matter for court. Legislature na dem dey make law, executive na dem dey carry out di law.

questions.q: In a presidential system like Nigeria's, which action best illustrates the principle of checks and balances between the legislature and the executive?
o: The executive alone decides the national budget without legislative input
The judiciary drafts bills for the legislature to debate
The legislature can override a presidential veto of a bill with a two-thirds majority vote
The President appoints all ministers without any form of approval
questions.e: Checks and balances allow one arm of government to limit the power of another. When the legislature overrides a presidential veto with a two-thirds majority, it is checking the power of the executive, which is a classic example of this principle.
questions.p: Checks and balances mean say one arm of government fit control di oda one power. If legislature use two-third majority override President veto, dem dey check di executive power, and dat na correct example.

questions.q: Who heads the executive arm of government at the federal level in Nigeria?
o: The Senate President
The Speaker of the House of Representatives
The Chief Justice of Nigeria
The President
questions.e: The President is the head of the executive arm of government at the federal level in Nigeria, responsible for implementing laws and policies. The Chief Justice heads the judiciary, while the Senate President and Speaker lead the legislature.
questions.p: President na di head of executive for federal level for Nigeria, na im dey implement law and policy. Chief Justice na for judiciary, Senate President and Speaker na for legislature.

questions.q: In a certain country, the President suddenly removes all Supreme Court judges and replaces them with people loyal to him, without following any laid-down constitutional procedure. Which democratic principle is clearly being violated?
o: Independence of the judiciary
Fiscal federalism
Bicameralism
Ministerial responsibility
questions.e: Independence of the judiciary means courts and judges should be free from control or interference by the executive or legislature. Removing judges arbitrarily to install loyalists directly attacks this independence, undermining fair justice.
questions.p: Independence of judiciary mean say court and judge suppose free from executive or legislature control. If President dey comot judges anyhow to put im loyalists, e dey spoil dis independence and e no go fit give fair justice again.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function performed by the executive arm of government?
o: Conducting foreign relations with other countries
Passing bills into law
Maintaining law and order in the state
Implementing government policies
questions.e: Passing bills into law is the work of the legislature, not the executive; the executive only gives assent to bills already passed. The other options -implementing policies, maintaining law and order, and foreign relations - are proper executive functions.
questions.p: To pass bill into law na legislature work, executive just dey sign/assent to di bill wey don already pass. Di oda ones like implement policy, keep law and order, and foreign relations na correct executive work.

questions.q: In Lamidostan, the Minister of Finance privately instructs judges on how to rule in a tax case that is still pending in court. Which democratic principle is being breached by the Minister's action?
o: Fiscal federalism
Collective responsibility
Federal character principle
Separation of powers
questions.e: Separation of powers requires that each arm of government, including the judiciary, functions independently without undue interference from the other arms. An executive official instructing judges on a pending case directly breaches this principle by interfering in judicial matters.
questions.p: Separation of powers mean say each arm of government, including judiciary, suppose work independently without oda arm dey disturb am. If Minister dey instruct judge for case wey still dey court, na im dey break dis principle because e don enter judiciary business.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a public corporation?
o: A government-owned organisation set up by law to provide essential services to the public
A private business owned by shareholders purely for profit
A religious body that provides free education to its members
A cooperative society formed by workers to save money together
questions.e: A public corporation is created by an Act of government to run important services like electricity, transport or oil. It is owned and controlled by the state, not private individuals.
questions.p: Public corporation na organisation wey government create with law to give people important services. E be say government dey own am and control am, no be private pesin.

questions.q: A major reason why government establishes public corporations instead of leaving certain services to private individuals is to...
o: ensure that only wealthy citizens enjoy essential services
provide essential services that may be too costly or unattractive for private investors
reduce the responsibility of government towards its citizens
encourage foreign companies to monopolise the economy
questions.e: Services like railways, electricity and water need huge capital and may not bring quick profit, so private investors may avoid them. Government therefore sets up public corporations to make sure such services reach everybody.
questions.p: Some service like rail, light and water need plenty money and no dey bring quick profit, so private pesin fit avoid am. Na why government dey form public corporation make everybody fit get di service.

questions.q: A common problem associated with the management of public corporations in many West African countries is...
o: the refusal of citizens to make use of corporation services
the complete inability of government to appoint any staff at all
political interference in the day-to-day running of the corporation
too much competition from several private investors in the same sector
questions.e: Politicians sometimes interfere by appointing unqualified loyalists or dictating decisions for political gain, which weakens efficient management. This is a well-known challenge facing many public corporations in the region.
questions.p: Sometimes politician dey interfere for how dem dey run public corporation, like to put their own pesin wey no sabi work. Dis one dey cause bad management for many public corporation for West Africa.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the civil service from the public service?
o: The civil service covers only government ministries and departments, while the public service is a broader term that also includes public corporations and other state agencies
The public service refers only to the armed forces, while the civil service covers ministries alone
The civil service is owned by private investors while the public service is owned by government
There is no real difference; both terms refer to exactly the same narrow group of workers
questions.e: Civil service is a narrower term for workers directly in ministries and government departments carrying out policy. Public service is wider and includes civil servants plus workers in public corporations, the judiciary, the police and other state bodies.
questions.p: Civil service na only ministry and department workers wey dey carry out government policy. Public service big pass am, e include civil service plus public corporation, judiciary, police and oda government bodies.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common method used by government to control the activities of public corporations?
o: Selling all shares of the corporation to foreign companies as soon as it is formed
Allowing the management to operate without any reporting to government
Appointing a board of directors who report regularly to a supervising ministry
Preventing the corporation from employing any Nigerian citizens
questions.e: Government usually appoints a board of directors to manage the corporation, and this board reports to a ministry responsible for supervising its activities. This keeps the corporation accountable while allowing it some independence.
questions.p: Government dey appoint board of directors to manage di corporation, and dem go dey report to one ministry wey dey supervise am. Dis one dey make sure say di corporation dey accountable even though e get small freedom.

questions.q: The Federal Government's decision to sell some shares of a loss-making public corporation to private investors, in order to improve efficiency and reduce the burden on public funds, is best described as...
o: privatisation
decentralisation
federalism
nationalisation
questions.e: Privatisation means transferring ownership or control of a government-owned enterprise to private investors, usually to improve efficiency and cut government spending. This matches exactly what is described in the question.
questions.p: Privatisation na when government sell share or ownership of im company to private pesin, so dat di company go dey run better and government go spend less money for am. Na dat kain action dem dey describe for dis question.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the term 'local government' as used in Nigerian political studies?
o: An arm of the judiciary that settles land disputes
A system of government at the grassroots with power to manage local affairs
A committee set up by political parties to organise elections
A branch of the police force stationed in villages
questions.e: Local government is the third tier of government closest to the people, given power by law to manage affairs within a defined local area such as roads, markets and primary healthcare. The other options describe unrelated institutions.
questions.p: Local government na di government wey close pass to di common people, dem get power to manage local matters like roads and market. Di oda options no relate to dat.

questions.q: According to the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, how many local government areas are officially recognized?
questions.e: The 1999 Constitution lists 774 local government areas across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. 36 is the number of states, 109 is the number of senators, and 360 is the number of House of Representatives members.
questions.p: Di 1999 Constitution list 774 local government areas inside di 36 states and FCT. 36 na states, 109 na senators, 360 na House of Reps members, so dem no fit be di answer.

questions.q: In which year did Nigeria carry out the major local government reform that introduced a uniform single-tier system of local administration throughout the country?
questions.e: The 1976 local government reform, carried out under General Olusegun Obasanjo's military regime, created a single, uniform structure of local government across Nigeria for the first time. The other years relate to different political events such as coups and new constitutions.
questions.p: Na for 1976 Nigeria do dat big local government reform wey bring one uniform system across di whole country, under Obasanjo military government. Di oda years na different political events.

questions.q: Which of these is a major source of internally generated revenue for local governments in Nigeria?
o: Import duties on goods
Tenement rates on buildings
Petroleum profit tax
Company income tax
questions.e: Tenement rates, charged on buildings within the local area, are a common internal revenue source that local governments collect directly. Petroleum profit tax, company income tax and import duties are collected by the Federal Government.
questions.p: Tenement rate wey dem dey collect for buildings inside di local area na one common revenue source wey local government dey collect direct. Petroleum profit tax, company tax and import duty na Federal Government dey collect dem.

questions.q: The chief executive who heads the administration of a local government area in Nigeria is officially known as the?
o: Governor
Minister
Commissioner
Chairman
questions.e: The Chairman is the elected head of a local government council, similar to how a governor heads a state. Commissioners and ministers serve at state and federal levels respectively, not at the local government level.
questions.p: Chairman na im be di elected head of local government council, just as governor dey head state. Commissioner and minister na for state and federal level, no be local government.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary function performed by local governments in Nigeria?
o: Provision and maintenance of markets and motor parks
Printing and issuing of national currency
Formulation of the country's foreign policy
Establishment of federal high courts
questions.e: Local governments are responsible for local infrastructure such as markets, motor parks, and refuse disposal because these services directly affect daily community life. Foreign policy, currency printing and federal courts are federal government responsibilities.
questions.p: Local government dey responsible for local tins like market and motor park, and refuse wey affect community every day. Foreign policy, currency and federal courts na federal government business.

questions.q: Which of the following factors is most responsible for the weak financial independence of local governments in Nigeria, despite their constitutional recognition?
o: Low population of rural dwellers
Absence of local government secretariats
Lack of qualified staff in rural councils
The joint account arrangement with state governments
questions.e: Even though local governments are recognised by the constitution and have guaranteed allocations, the joint account system allows state governments to control and sometimes withhold these funds, weakening local financial independence. The other options are minor issues compared to this structural problem.
questions.p: Even though constitution recognize local government and give dem allocation, di joint account system make state government fit control or hold di money, and dis one dey weaken local government money power. Di oda options na small issues wey no reach dis structural wahala.

questions.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani political system, what title was given to the traditional ruler of an emirate?
o: Obi
Oba
Emir
Eze
questions.e: After Usman dan Fodio's jihad of 1804 established the Sokoto Caliphate, the ruler of each emirate under the Caliphate was called an Emir. This title replaced the earlier Hausa title of 'Sarki'.
questions.p: Afta di jihad wey Usman dan Fodio lead for 1804 wey bring Sokoto Caliphate, dem dey call di ruler of each emirate 'Emir'. Dis title take ova from di old Hausa title 'Sarki'.

questions.q: What title is given to the traditional ruler of a Yoruba kingdom such as Oyo or Ife?
o: Obi
Oba
Emir
Igwe
questions.e: In Yoruba land, the traditional ruler of a kingdom is called an Oba. He is seen as a sacred figure and the symbol of unity for his people.
questions.p: For Yoruba land, dem dey call di king of any kingdom 'Oba'. Dem dey see am as sacred person wey unite im pipo.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the pre-colonial Igbo political system compared to the Hausa-Fulani and Yoruba systems?
o: It was an acephalous system in which power was shared among councils of elders and age-grades
It was a caliphate controlled by a religious head
It was a centralized monarchy ruled by one king
It was a federation of emirates under one Sultan
questions.e: Unlike the Hausa-Fulani and Yoruba, who had centralized kingdoms, most Igbo communities had no single central ruler. Power was shared among elders, age-grades, title societies and village assemblies.
questions.p: Unlike Hausa-Fulani and Yoruba wey get central king, most Igbo community no get one central ruler. Dem dey share power among elders, age-grade, title societies and village meeting.

questions.q: Who led the Islamic jihad of 1804 that overthrew the Hausa kings and led to the establishment of the Sokoto Caliphate?
o: Muhammadu Rumfa
Usman dan Fodio
Ahmadu Bello
Mungo Park
questions.e: Usman dan Fodio, a Fulani Islamic scholar, led the 1804 jihad against the Hausa kings for practising what he saw as impure Islam. This led to the creation of the Sokoto Caliphate.
questions.p: Usman dan Fodio, Fulani Islamic teacher, lead di 1804 jihad against Hausa kings wey im claim say dem no dey practise correct Islam. Na dis jihad bring Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.q: In the Old Oyo Empire, which body of chiefs had the power to check the excesses of the Alaafin and could present him with an empty calabash or parrot eggs as a sign that he should end his own life?
o: Oyo Mesi
Ogboni society
Ilari (palace messengers)
Egbe Omo Oduduwa
questions.e: The Oyo Mesi, led by the Bashorun, was a council of seven senior chiefs who acted as a check on the Alaafin's power. If he became tyrannical, they could present him with symbols demanding that he take his own life.
questions.p: Oyo Mesi, wey Bashorun dey lead, na council of seven senior chiefs wey dey check di Alaafin power. If e start to dey do wayo rulership, dem fit give am sign make e kill imself.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the pre-colonial Igbo political system is often described as 'republican' compared to the Hausa-Fulani and Yoruba systems?
o: Igbo villages paid tribute to one central emperor who controlled them all
Igbo rulers were appointed directly by Islamic clerics as in the Sokoto Caliphate
Igbo communities were ruled only by hereditary kings from royal families
Political authority among the Igbo was shared among elders, age-grades and title-holders rather than concentrated in one hereditary ruler
questions.e: A republican system spreads power among many people instead of one ruler. Since Igbo authority rested with councils of elders, age-grades and title societies rather than a single hereditary monarch, it is called republican, unlike the centralized Hausa-Fulani and Yoruba monarchies.
questions.p: Republican system na when power dey spread among plenty pipo instead of one ruler. Since Igbo authority dey with elders, age-grade and title societies instead of one hereditary king, dem dey call am republican, unlike Hausa-Fulani and Yoruba wey get central king.

questions.q: Among the riverine Igbo communities such as Onitsha, unlike most other Igbo areas, the traditional ruler bears which title, showing some monarchical influence?
o: Oba
Oloye
Obi
Emir
questions.e: Onitsha and some neighbouring riverine Igbo communities, influenced by contact with Benin and Igala, developed a more centralized kingship and call their ruler 'Obi', unlike the acephalous structure of most Igbo towns.
questions.p: Onitsha and some riverine Igbo town, because of dia contact with Benin and Igala, get more central kingship and dem dey call dia ruler 'Obi', unlike oda Igbo town wey no get central king.

questions.q: In the Hausa language, what does the traditional title 'Sarki', used before the Islamic reforms introduced the title of Emir, mean?
o: Military general
Village head
King or supreme ruler
Chief priest
questions.e: Before Usman dan Fodio's jihad, the Hausa states were ruled by kings called 'Sarki', meaning king or supreme ruler of a Hausa state. After the jihad, the title Emir was introduced for rulers under the Sokoto Caliphate.
questions.p: Before Usman dan Fodio jihad, Hausa states dey ruled by kings wey dem dey call 'Sarki', wey mean king or supreme ruler. Afta di jihad, dem bring di title 'Emir' for rulers under Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.q: Indirect rule, the system of using existing traditional rulers to administer colonies on behalf of the British, was mainly introduced and developed in Nigeria by:
o: Lord Lugard
Hugh Clifford
Arthur Richards
Oliver Lyttleton
questions.e: Lord Lugard first used indirect rule in Northern Nigeria and later extended it to other parts of the country. The other men were later colonial governors linked to different constitutions, not the founder of indirect rule.
questions.p: Na Lord Lugard first use indirect rule for Northern Nigeria before im later spread am give other areas. Di oda men na governors wey later bring different constitutions, dem no be di one wey start am.

questions.q: In Northern Nigeria, the British carried out indirect rule mainly through the existing:
o: Resident Commissioners
Warrant Chiefs
District Officers
Emirs
questions.e: The North already had a centralized Emirate system, so the British ruled through the Emirs who collected taxes and kept law and order for them. Warrant Chiefs were used in the East, not the North.
questions.p: Northern Nigeria don get strong Emirate system before, so British use di Emirs rule di people, dem go collect tax and keep order. Warrant Chiefs na for Eastern Nigeria dem use.

questions.q: A major reason indirect rule did not work well in many parts of Eastern Nigeria was that the area:
o: rejected all European goods
lacked centralized traditional rulers like the emirs in the North
