had no contact with the British at all
produced no cash crops for trade
questions.e: Most Igbo communities were organised in small, independent village groups without powerful central chiefs, unlike the Emirates in the North. This made it hard for the British to find suitable local rulers to use for indirect rule.
questions.p: Most Igbo communities na small village wey dey rule demsef, dem no get one big central chief like di Emirs for North. Dis one make am hard for British to find correct local ruler to use run indirect rule.

questions.q: The artificial chiefs created by the British in Eastern Nigeria, who had no traditional authority but were given power to collect tax and judge cases, were called:
o: Warrant Chiefs
District Heads
Resident Officers
Emirs
questions.e: Because the East had no central chiefs, the British appointed some men as Warrant Chiefs and gave them a warrant (certificate) of authority. Many of these men were not respected traditional leaders, which caused resentment.
questions.p: Since East no get central chief, British pick some men give dem 'warrant' (paper) of power, dem call dem Warrant Chiefs. Many of dis men no be real traditional leader, so people vex plenty.

questions.q: The unpopular Warrant Chief system and fear of new taxation on women in Eastern Nigeria eventually led to the:
o: Lagos Treaty of Cession
Berlin Conference
Amalgamation of 1914
Aba Women's Riot of 1929
questions.e: Women in Aba and nearby towns protested in 1929 against the Warrant Chiefs and the rumour that the British wanted to tax women, leading to the famous Aba Women's Riot. The other events are unrelated to this protest.
questions.p: Women for Aba and nearby towns vex for 1929 because of Warrant Chiefs and rumour say British wan tax women, dis one bring di famous Aba Women Riot. Di oda events no connect to dis protest.

questions.q: The event in which the British joined the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria into one country took place in the year:
questions.e: Lord Lugard carried out the amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates in 1914, creating the single colony known as Nigeria. This is a well known fixed date in Nigerian colonial history.
questions.p: Na for 1914 Lord Lugard join Northern and Southern Protectorates together make dem be one Nigeria. Dis date na correct well known fact for Nigerian history.

questions.q: Among the colonial constitutions, the one that first divided Nigeria into regions (North, East and West) for administrative and representative purposes was the:
o: Clifford Constitution of 1922
Macpherson Constitution of 1951
Richards Constitution of 1946
Lyttleton Constitution of 1954
questions.e: The Richards Constitution of 1946 is remembered for introducing regionalism by creating Regional Houses of Assembly for the North, East and West. The Clifford Constitution came before regionalism, while Macpherson and Lyttleton came after and built on it.
questions.p: Richards Constitution of 1946 na im first bring regionalism, e create Regional House of Assembly for North, East and West. Clifford Constitution come before regionalism start, while Macpherson and Lyttleton come later build on top am.

questions.q: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 is best remembered in Nigerian history for:
o: ending indirect rule completely across Nigeria
establishing a true federal system with regions having separate legislative lists
granting Nigeria full independence from Britain
introducing the first Legislative Council in Nigeria
questions.e: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 made Nigeria a proper federation, giving the Regions their own legislative powers over certain matters (regional list) while the centre kept others. It did not end indirect rule or grant independence, and the Legislative Council existed long before 1954.
questions.p: Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 make Nigeria become real federation, e give Regions power to make law for some matters wey be regional list, while centre still hold im own. E no end indirect rule or give independence, and Legislative Council don dey before 1954 sef.

questions.q: Which notable Nigerian nationalist founded the West African Pilot newspaper, which was widely used to campaign against colonial rule and spread nationalist ideas among Nigerians?
o: Herbert Macaulay
Obafemi Awolowo
Ahmadu Bello
Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.e: Nnamdi Azikiwe founded the West African Pilot in 1937 and used it to criticise colonial rule and awaken nationalist consciousness in Nigerians.
questions.p: Na Nnamdi Azikiwe start West African Pilot for 1937, e dey use am criticize colonial government and wake up nationalist feeling for Nigerians.

questions.q: Which Nigerian constitution, introduced in 1922, first allowed a small number of educated Nigerians in Lagos and Calabar to elect their own representatives into the Legislative Council?
o: Richards Constitution
Macpherson Constitution
Clifford Constitution
Lyttleton Constitution
questions.e: The 1922 Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle, allowing Lagos and Calabar to elect a few members into the Legislative Council for the first time.
questions.p: Na Clifford Constitution of 1922 bring elective principle, wey make Lagos and Calabar fit elect small members enter Legislative Council for the first time.

questions.q: Which constitution, introduced in 1946, first divided Nigeria into three regions (Northern, Eastern and Western) and created regional houses of assembly?
o: Richards Constitution
Clifford Constitution
Macpherson Constitution
Lyttleton Constitution
questions.e: The Richards Constitution of 1946 divided Nigeria into three regions and set up regional houses, laying the foundation for the federal system Nigeria later adopted.
questions.p: Na Richards Constitution of 1946 first divide Nigeria into three regions and bring regional houses, na im start the federal arrangement Nigeria later take.

questions.q: A key feature of the 1954 Lyttleton Constitution was that it...
o: introduced a strong federal system with each region enjoying self-government in internal affairs
abolished political parties in Nigeria
handed full independence to Nigeria
merged the three regions into a single unitary state
questions.e: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 firmly established federalism, granting each region control over its own internal affairs while a central government handled common national matters.
questions.p: Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 bring strong federal system, where every region fit control dia own internal matter while central government dey handle common national issues.

questions.q: The Action Group (AG), led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo, drew its strongest political support mainly from which group of Nigerians?
o: Igbo in the East
Hausa-Fulani in the North
Yoruba in the West
Efik in Calabar
questions.e: The Action Group was formed in 1951 mainly to champion the political and cultural interests of the Yoruba-speaking people of Western Nigeria.
questions.p: Action Group, wey Awolowo lead, get im main support from Yoruba people for Western Nigeria.

questions.q: In 1953, Chief Anthony Enahoro moved a motion in the House of Representatives calling for Nigeria's self-government by 1956. Opposition to this motion by which party led to a walkout and eventually sparked riots in Kano?
o: United Middle Belt Congress (UMBC)
Northern Peoples Congress (NPC)
National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
Action Group (AG)
questions.e: Northern leaders in the NPC felt the North was not yet ready for self-government by 1956, so they opposed the motion and walked out of the House, a disagreement that later led to the 1953 Kano riots.
questions.p: Northern leaders for NPC no gree with the 1956 self-government motion, dem argue say North never ready, dem waka comot for House, and the tension later cause Kano riot for 1953.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT a major factor that encouraged the rise of nationalism in colonial Nigeria?
o: Spread of Western education
Impact of the Second World War on colonial subjects
Racial discrimination by colonial officials
Formation of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
questions.e: ECOWAS was formed in 1975, well after Nigeria gained independence in 1960, so it could not have caused the earlier nationalist agitation; the other options were genuine pre-independence influences.
questions.p: ECOWAS start for 1975, afta Nigeria don independent since 1960, so e no fit be one of the things wey cause nationalism before independence; the other options na real factors wey cause am.

questions.q: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), founded in 1944, was initially formed mainly to...
o: oversee local government elections in Lagos
unite Nigerians and Cameroonians in the struggle for better political and economic conditions
draft Nigeria's independence constitution
organize the first military coup in Nigeria
questions.e: The NCNC was founded in 1944 as a pressure group to unite Nigerians and Cameroonians under British rule to press for political and economic reforms and later self-government.
questions.p: Dem form NCNC for 1944 as pressure group make Nigerians and Cameroonians unite fight together for better political and economic condition, and later self-government.

questions.q: On what date did Nigeria officially gain independence from British colonial rule?
o: January 15, 1966
October 1, 1979
October 1, 1960
October 1, 1963
questions.e: Nigeria became an independent nation on October 1, 1960, though it remained a dominion under the British monarch until 1963. This date marks the end of direct colonial rule.
questions.p: Naija get independence on October 1, 1960. E still dey under British Queen small-small until 1963 when e become republic proper.

questions.q: In which year did Nigeria officially become a republic, replacing the British monarch with an indigenous Head of State?
questions.e: Nigeria became a republic on October 1, 1963, with Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe as the first indigenous President, though Nigeria had gained independence earlier in 1960.
questions.p: Na 1963 Naija become republic, and Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe be di first President. Independence come before dat one for 1960.

questions.q: Which event of January 1966 brought the Nigerian First Republic to an abrupt end?
o: The declaration of the Republic of Biafra
The declaration of a state of emergency in the Western Region
The formation of the NPC-NCNC coalition
The first military coup led by young army officers
questions.e: On January 15, 1966, a group of young army officers led a coup that toppled the civilian government of the First Republic, killing several top politicians and military leaders. This marked the beginning of military rule in Nigeria.
questions.p: On January 15, 1966, young army officers do coup wey finish di First Republic civilian government. Na dis one start military rule for Naija.

questions.q: What was the immediate cause of the Nigerian Civil War that lasted from 1967 to 1970?
o: The Eastern Region declared itself an independent state known as Biafra
The Western Region demanded secession from the federation
The Northern Region refused to join the federation
The Mid-Western Region demanded creation of more states
questions.e: Following the pogroms against Igbos and political tensions, the Eastern Region under Lt Col Odumegwu Ojukwu declared independence as the Republic of Biafra in 1967, leading to a civil war with the federal government.
questions.p: After di killings of Igbo people and political wahala, Eastern Region under Ojukwu declare demsef as Biafra for 1967. Na dis cause di civil war with Federal Government.

questions.q: Who, as Military Head of State, annulled the June 12, 1993 presidential election widely believed to have been won by Chief MKO Abiola?
o: Sani Abacha
Ernest Shonekan
Abdulsalami Abubakar
Ibrahim Babangida
questions.e: General Ibrahim Babangida, who was Head of State at the time, annulled the June 12, 1993 election, triggering a major political crisis that eventually led to his stepping aside later that year.
questions.p: Na General Ibrahim Babangida, wey be Head of State at dat time, cancel di June 12, 1993 election. Dis action cause big political wahala wey make am step aside later dat year.

questions.q: On what date did Nigeria formally return to civilian democratic rule after years of military governance, with Olusegun Obasanjo being inaugurated as President?
o: January 1, 1999
December 31, 1998
October 1, 1999
questions.e: Nigeria returned to democratic rule on May 29, 1999, when Olusegun Obasanjo was sworn in as President, marking the start of the Fourth Republic.
questions.p: Naija return to democracy on May 29, 1999, when Olusegun Obasanjo take oath as President. Dis start di Fourth Republic.

questions.q: Historians generally agree that one major reason military regimes repeatedly took over power during Nigeria's First and Second Republics was that:
o: The constitution specifically allowed the military to govern every ten years
Civilian leaders invited the military to rule as advisers
Widespread corruption, electoral malpractice and inter-ethnic political crises weakened civilian governments
The United Nations mandated military oversight of Nigeria's democracy
questions.e: Both the First and Second Republics suffered from rigged elections, corrupt practices and deep ethnic/regional rivalries, which weakened public confidence in civilian rule and gave the military an excuse to intervene. There was no constitutional or international mandate for military rule.
questions.p: Both First and Second Republic suffer from election rigging, corruption and ethnic wahala, wey weaken people trust for civilian government. Na dis kind situation give military excuse to enter power, no be say constitution or UN order am.

questions.q: Which administration is credited with starting the transition programme that eventually produced the 1979 Constitution and handed power to the civilian Second Republic?
o: The Murtala Mohammed/Olusegun Obasanjo regime
Yakubu Gowon's administration
Muhammadu Buhari's regime
Ibrahim Babangida's regime
questions.e: General Murtala Mohammed began the transition programme in 1975, and after his assassination in 1976, General Olusegun Obasanjo continued it, leading to the 1979 Constitution and handover to Shehu Shagari's civilian government.
questions.p: General Murtala Mohammed start di transition programme for 1975, and after dem kill am for 1976, Obasanjo continue am. Na dis bring di 1979 Constitution and handover to Shehu Shagari civilian government.

questions.q: Which principle of Nigeria's foreign policy places the welfare and interest of Africa at the very centre of all international decisions taken by Nigeria?
o: Dependency
Non-alignment
Afrocentrism
Economic diplomacy
questions.e: Afrocentrism means Africa is the main focus of Nigeria's foreign policy. Nigeria sees itself as a leader that must protect African interests first. This is why Nigeria has supported liberation struggles across Africa.
questions.p: Afrocentrism na di belief wey Africa dey for centre of Nigeria foreign affairs. Nigeria dey always put African interest first before anything. Na why Nigeria don help many African kontri wey dey fight for freedom.

questions.q: The government agency directly responsible for conducting Nigeria's day-to-day diplomatic relations with other countries and international organisations is the
o: Federal Executive Council
National Assembly
Code of Conduct Bureau
Ministry of Foreign Affairs
questions.e: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs handles embassies, treaties, and relations with other nations on behalf of Nigeria. It implements the foreign policy decided by the government. The other bodies have different, unrelated roles.
questions.p: Na Ministry of Foreign Affairs dey handle Nigeria relationship with oda kontri. Dem dey manage embassy, agreement and wetin concern foreign affairs. Di oda options no get dat kind work.

questions.q: Nigeria's foreign policy is sometimes explained using the idea of 'concentric circles'. In this model, which group forms the innermost circle that Nigeria must protect first?
o: The Commonwealth of Nations
Nigeria itself, its citizens and national interest
The wider international community
West Africa and the ECOWAS sub-region
questions.e: The concentric circle model places Nigeria's own survival and interest at the centre before widening outward to West Africa, Africa, and the rest of the world. Every country protects itself first before helping others. This is why national interest is the first circle.
questions.p: Di concentric circle idea show say Nigeria go first protect herself and her citizens before e go reach oda circles. Na from inside dey go dey expand go West Africa, Africa, den di whole world. National interest always come first.

questions.q: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was formed mainly to achieve what objective among member states?
o: Military conquest of neighbouring states
Abolition of all national currencies
Economic cooperation and regional integration
Religious unity across West Africa
questions.e: ECOWAS was set up in 1975 to promote trade, free movement of goods and people, and economic development among West African countries. It is not a military or religious body, though it later developed a peacekeeping arm. Economic cooperation remains its core goal.
questions.p: ECOWAS na organisation wey dem form for 1975 make West African kontri fit work togeda for economy. Di main goal na trade, free movement of people and development. E no be religion or military group, even though e later get peacekeeping arm.

questions.q: During the civil wars in Liberia and Sierra Leone, Nigeria led a West African peacekeeping force that helped restore order in those countries. This force was known as
o: ECOMOG
NATO West Africa
UN Blue Helmets Nigeria
AU Peace Force
questions.e: ECOMOG (ECOWAS Monitoring Group) was formed by ECOWAS, with Nigeria contributing the largest number of troops and funds. It intervened to stop the fighting in Liberia and Sierra Leone in the 1990s. This showed Nigeria's leadership role in regional peacekeeping.
questions.p: ECOMOG na di peacekeeping force wey ECOWAS form, and Nigeria give di highest number of soldiers and money. Dem go Liberia and Sierra Leone to stop di war for 1990s. Dis show say Nigeria dey lead for regional peace matter.

questions.q: During the Cold War, Nigeria chose a non-aligned foreign policy instead of joining either the Western (capitalist) bloc or the Eastern (communist) bloc. What is the best reason for this choice?
o: Nigeria lacked enough soldiers to fight a war
Nigeria was forbidden by the United Nations from choosing sides
Nigeria had no diplomats trained in foreign affairs
Nigeria wanted to avoid being used as a tool by either superpower and to protect its independent interests
questions.e: Non-alignment allowed Nigeria to relate freely with both blocs without being controlled by either superpower's interest. This protected Nigeria's sovereignty and gave it freedom to make independent decisions in international affairs. The other options are not the real reasons behind this policy.
questions.p: Non-alignment mean say Nigeria no go join eida side so dat superpowers no go control am. Dis one protect Nigeria independence and give am freedom to make e own decision for world matter. Di oda options no be di real reason.

questions.q: Shortly after gaining independence in 1960, Nigeria immediately became a member of which world body, showing its early commitment to global peace and cooperation?
o: The World Bank Group
The United Nations
The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation
The European Union
questions.e: Nigeria joined the United Nations in October 1960, the same year it gained independence from Britain. This showed Nigeria's willingness to be part of the global community and contribute to world peace. The European Union and NATO are regional groupings that Nigeria, as an African country, cannot join.
questions.p: Nigeria join United Nations for October 1960, di same year e gain independence. Dis show say Nigeria wan dey part of world community and support world peace. European Union and NATO na regional group wey Nigeria no fit join.
